judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain payment schedule: five $300,000 instalments beginning January 2, 2010 totalling exactly $1.5 million, memorialised by a note substantially in the form of Exhibit A; the arithmetic and dates are internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A is not attached to the instrument, and Section IX (c015) limits the remedy for non-completion to refiling, which could be argued to swallow the note obligation, but nothing directly contradicts the payment terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The embedded stipulation that the MOU 'is sufficiently definite to allow the parties to sue for its enforcement' is a self-serving legal conclusion sitting in a document full of agreements to agree, and 'tolling and other litigation resumption agreements' is left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely collides with Section IX (c015), which says that if the required actions are not completed Lincoln's remedy 'shall be to refile the lawsuit' — enforceability of the MOU versus a single restoration-of-the-status-quo remedy is the obvious construction fight here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tolling period reads 'for five (5) years of until all claims ... have been paid and settled', where the mangled 'of/or' leaves it unclear whether five years is a floor, a cap, or an alternative to the claims-run-off date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Section V (c011)'s promised 'tolling and other litigation resumption agreements' and Section IX (c015)'s refiling remedy; the tolling term is what makes refiling meaningful, so the fit is supportive rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to regulatory approval' names no regulator, no applicant, no deadline and no consequence of refusal, and 'the matters to which it addresses' is undefined — a short clause with a large unresolved boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be easily squared with Section V (c011), where dismissal follows on execution and the MOU is declared immediately enforceable, nor with the fixed June 30, 2009 deadlines in Sections I and II (c005, c007).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard joint-drafting clause disclaiming contra proferentem; its wording is conventional and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on how every other clause is read but contradicts none; nothing elsewhere in the MOU identifies a drafter or reserves construction against one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading covers failure to complete 'or Later Breach' but the body addresses only non-completion, and 'Lincoln's remedy shall be to refile the lawsuit' does not say whether it is the sole and exclusive remedy; the illustrative 'such as ... including but not limited to' list adds further scope uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Directly opposed to Section V (c011)'s statement that the MOU is definite enough to sue on, and it would also strip content from the payment and security obligations in Sections II and IV (c007, c010) — the central whole-instrument tension in this document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is an agreement to draft a future settlement agreement whose terms — 'among other things', 'the particulars of the releases ... shall be set forth in the settlement agreement' — are expressly left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Releases of all Defendants sit against Section III (c009), which preserves the other defendants' obligations, and against Section IX (c015), which treats failure to reach this very agreement as merely restoring the lawsuit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary counterparts and facsimile-execution boilerplate; the terms are conventional and unambiguous despite scanning noise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section V (c011), which turns on 'execution of this Memorandum of Understanding'; no other clause addresses execution formalities differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A further-assurances clause qualified by 'reasonably necessary', which is a familiar standard rather than a genuine ambiguity, though it is run together with the counterparts section and carries a duplicated section number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the specific future-document duties in Sections I, IX and X (c005, c015, c016); a party could argue it independently compels execution of the LPT or settlement agreement notwithstanding the refiling-only remedy.
